วัดนิกรวราราม หรือวัดย่านยาว เริ่มสร้างใ: Wat Nikorn Wararam, or Wat Yan Yao, was initially built in 1793 (2336 BE) by Ta Kaeo and Ta Ram. The found evidence verifies the year and the names of the initiators, but does not state the detailed reason for establishing the temple for any specific mission. Therefore, this temple should be read as a religious site of the local community forming in the Takua Pa basin, rather than tying it to unverified narratives.
เมืองตะกั่วป่าในภาพกว้างมีประวัติเป็นเมื: Takua Pa in the broad picture has a history as a port town and tin mining source, with maritime trade and various groups of people. However, no temple-specific evidence has been found to verify the role of Wat Nikorn Wararam in tin mining, maritime trade, Hokkien Chinese, or the town governor system. Thus, no conclusion is made beyond the sources.

However, no documents have been found specifying major restorations, changes of hands, or abandoned periods.
หลังสึนามิวันที่ 26 ธันวาคม 2547 วัดถูกใ: After the tsunami on 26 December 2004 (2547 BE), the temple was used as a site to gather victims' bodies awaiting victim identification. This temporary role made Wat Yan Yao a part of Takua Pa's disaster response history. Later, on 30 October 2022 (2565 BE), Samnakngan Phraphutthasatsana Changwat Phangnga (Phang Nga Provincial Office of Buddhism) jointly handed over the land title deed documents to the abbot, serving as evidence of modern land ownership management.
